paragraphs: HireQuest, Inc. (collectively with its subsidiaries, the "Company," "we," "us," or "our") is a Delaware corporation originally organized in Washington as Command Staffing, LLC in 2002. In 2005, Temporary Financial Services, Inc., a public company, acquired the assets of Command Staffing, LLC, and the combined entity changed its name to Command Center, Inc. On September 11, 2019, Command Center, Inc. reincorporated in Delaware and changed its name to HireQuest, Inc. following its acquisition of Hire Quest Holdings, LLC ("Hire Quest Holdings," and together with its subsidiary, Hire Quest, LLC, "Legacy HQ"). This acquisition is sometimes referred to as the "Merger." Hire Quest, LLC was formed as a Florida limited liability company in 2002. Hire Quest Holdings, LLC was formed as a Florida limited liability company in 2017. Since the Merger, we have made a number of acquisitions which are discussed in more detail below.
Our common stock trades on the Nasdaq Market under the symbol "HQI." All references to "common stock" means the common stock of HireQuest, Inc., par value $0.001 per share.

Our principal executive office is located at 111 Springhall Drive, Goose Creek, SC, 29445 and the telephone number is (843) 723-7400. More information about us may be found at www.hirequest.com. The information on our website is not incorporated by reference in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

On December 4, 2023 we completed our acquisition of ten locations of TEC Staffing Services ("TEC") in Arkansas in accordance with the terms of an Asset Purchase Agreement dated October 23, 2023 for approximately $9.8 million. TEC has been a provider of industrial staffing services to the employers and workers in Northwest and Central Arkansas for over 40 years. We funded this acquisition with existing cash on hand and a draw on our existing line of credit. We immediately entered into three franchise agreements with existing franchisees and sold the operating assets we acquired.

On December 30, 2024 we completed our acquisition of one location of Ready Temporary Services ("RTS") in Denver, Colorado in accordance with the terms of an Asset Purchase Agreement dated December 13, 2024 for $1.4 million. RTS has been a provider of day labor and industrial staffing services to the employers and workers of Denver, Colorado for multiple decades. We funded this acquisition with cash on hand and a draw on our existing line of credit. We immediately entered into a franchise agreement and sold the non-working capital assets we acquired.

On December 1, 2025, HQ MRI Corporation ("HQ MRI"), a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company entered into a contribution agreement (the "Contribution Agreement") with MRINetwork Operations, LLC ("MRI Operations") with an effective date of January 1, 2026 (the "Effective Date"). Pursuant to the Contribution Agreement, HQ MRI agreed to transfer, and MRI Operations agreed to accept, certain assets and liabilities associated with the MRINetwork as of the Effective Date in exchange for MRI Operations issuing to HQ MRI 40% of the ownership units of MRI Operations. HQ MRI contributed the non-contract staffing assets of MRINetwork necessary to carry on its day-to-day activities, the franchise agreements with franchisees of the MRINetwork, contracts with vendors and service providers, all claims against third parties related to the contributed assets, warranty, indemnity, and other similar rights related to the contributed assets, contracts with employees of HQ MRI, and other ancillary assets. MRI Operations also assumed accrued but unpaid payroll and benefits for employees of the network, all liabilities arising from the day-to-day activities of the network including accounts payable, and all liabilities relating to the contributed assets. The remaining 60% of MRI Operations is owned by an individual and four current franchisees of the MRINetwork. This transaction closed on January 1, 2026. The contract-staffing assets of the MRINetwork were not transferred as part of the transaction and were wholly retained by HQ MRI.

We are a nationwide franchisor of temporary staffing offices providing direct-dispatch and commercial staffing solutions in the light industrial and blue-collar industries, and professional recruitment offices providing permanent placement services in the executive, managerial and administrative fields. Following the Merger, we began with a strong direct-dispatch program. With the Snelling Acquisition and the LINK Acquisition, we significantly expanded our traditional commercial staffing solutions.

Smaller acquisitions have helped us fill our footprint and provide our franchisees and customers with one targeted offerings. These tuck in acquisitions have also served to bolster our existing services in certain geographic regions.

In 2025, our franchisees operated under the trade names "HireQuest Direct," "Snelling," "DriverQuest," "HireQuest Health," "Northbound Executive Search," "Management Recruiters International," "TradeCorp" and "Sales Consultants." HireQuest Direct focuses on daily-work/daily-pay jobs primarily for construction and light industrial customers. Snelling and HireQuest focus on longer-term staffing positions in the light industrial and administrative arenas. TradeCorp focuses on jobs primarily for construction site skilled trades. DriverQuest specializes in both commercial and non-CDL drivers serving a variety of industries and applications. HireQuest Health specializes in skilled personnel in the healthcare and dental industries. Northbound, MRI, and Sales Consultants focus on executive, managerial, and professional recruitment services, although many franchisees also offer short-term consultant and contract staffing services.

Our revenue, which is primarily comprised of royalty fees generated by the operations of our franchised offices, license fees, and interest charged to our franchisees on overdue accounts receivable, was $30.6 million in 2025. This does not include revenue from locations currently owned by us as those are classified as held-for-sale and reported as discontinued operations. Our system-wide sales, which we define as sales at all offices, whether owned and operated by us or by our franchisees, were $500.2 million in 2025. Nearly all system-wide sales originated from franchisee-owned offices. We employed approximately 75 thousand temporary employees and contracted with 85 independent contractors during 2025. At December 31, 2025, we had 413 franchisee-owned offices and one company-owned office operating in 43 states, the District of Columbia, and 14 countries outside the United States. 197 of those offices operated by 177 franchisees were MRI offices which were divested to MRINetwork Operations, LLC on January 1, 2026. On a net basis, we closed 12 offices in 2025 (acquiring or adding 7 and closing 19). In addition, there were 16 MRI locations that provided contract staffing services only.

We provide incentives to our existing franchisees, including assistance with start-up funding and acquisition costs, to encourage them to expand into new markets and industries. While staffing industry growth has outpaced overall economic and employment growth, the industry still employs only a small percentage of the United States' non-farm workforce. We believe that the low percentage of the total workforce that is currently contingent, when combined with potential shifts towards a more contingent workforce in the overall economy, provides meaningful opportunities for future organic growth.
Our differentiated services are driven by three key elements:

Local ownership and dedicated responsiveness. Our offices are franchisee-owned. We believe that ownership at the local level, where the vast majority of customer interactions occur, allows our organization to be agile and responsive to customer needs. Since our franchisees have a personal financial interest in the success of their offices, our customers interact with a representative who is incentivized to deliver excellent customer service and resolve issues efficiently. In addition, franchise owners are able to develop long-term relationships due to the lack of turnover. We believe the combination of local ownership coupled with properly-aligned incentives results in enhanced customer satisfaction and greater customer retention.

Direct dispatch from our offices. The majority of our employees in our construction and light industrial segment are dispatched from our offices every day. This allows our franchisees and their staff to qualify the employees for work, provide them with any necessary personal protective equipment, assist them in arranging transportation amongst themselves, and ensure the right number of qualified individuals are dispatched at the right time. We believe that employee dispatch from franchise offices increases consistency as our employees are sent to a particular jobsite without having to rely on less reliable means of verification, such as telephone calls. Once we and our customers have developed a rapport with particular employees, we will sometimes dispatch these employees directly to a customer location.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business and Industry
Acquisitions may have an adverse effect on our business.
New business initiatives will cause us to incur additional expenditures and may have an adverse effect on our core business.
We have been and may continue to be unable to attract sufficient qualified candidates to meet all of the needs of our clients.
We are vulnerable to seasonal fluctuations with lower demand in the winter months.
We are dependent on a small number of individuals who constitute our current management.
Our operating and financial results are largely linked to our large workers' compensation reserve which can be volatile.
We may incur employment related claims or other types of claims and costs that could materially harm our business.

If we fail successfully to implement our growth strategy, which includes new office development by existing and new franchisees, our ability to increase our revenue and operating profits could be adversely affected.
Changes in our industry could place strains on our management, employees, information systems, and internal controls, which may adversely impact our business.
Shifts in attitudes towards contingent workforces could negatively impact our results of operations and financial condition.
Risks Related to our Credit Facility and Liquidity
Our level of debt and restrictions in our credit agreement could negatively affect our operations and limit our liquidity and our ability to react to changes in the economy.
In addition, the line of credit agreement limits, among other things, our ability to:
Without sufficient liquidity, we may not be able to pursue accretive business opportunities.
We may be unable to obtain financing of our working capital, acquisition, capital, dividend, and other needs on favorable terms.
Risks Related to Our Franchisees and Business Model
Converting company-owned offices to franchises has multiple risks.
Our operating and financial results and growth strategies are closely tied to the success of our franchisees.
Our franchisees could take action that could harm our business.
If we fail to identify, recruit, and contract with a sufficient number of qualified franchisees, our ability to open new offices and increase our revenue could be materially adversely affected.
Opening new offices in existing markets and aggressive development could cannibalize existing sales and may negatively affect sales at existing offices and relationships with existing franchisees.
A large number of our franchises are controlled by a small number of individuals.
Our results of operations may be significantly affected by the ability of certain franchisees to repay their loans to us.
Our growth strategy is reliant on finding purchasers for assets of the businesses we acquire.
We may have improperly balanced the costs and benefits related to our Franchise Expansion Incentive Program.
Risks Related to Technology and Cybersecurity
The improper disclosure of or access to our confidential and proprietary information, or a failure to adequately protect this information, could materially harm our business.

Our information technology systems may need to be updated or replaced which may be disruptive and expensive. If we fail to update or replace our information technology systems as needed, our business could be harmed.
Advances in technology may disrupt the labor and recruiting markets.
Our facilities, operations, and information technology systems may be vulnerable to damage and interruption.
Risks Related to Ownership of Our Stock
If we are a "personal holding company," we may be required to pay personal holding company taxes, which would have an adverse effect on our cash flows, results of operations, and financial condition.
Our directors, officers, and current principal stockholders own a large percentage of our common stock and could limit other stockholders' influence over corporate decisions.
Our stock typically trades in low volumes daily which could lead to illiquidity, volatility, or depressed stock price.
Analysts covering our stock could negatively impact both the stock price and trading volume of our stock.
If we cease paying cash dividends on our common stock, you may not receive any return on investment unless you sell your common stock for a price greater than that which you paid for it.

We are a "smaller reporting company" as defined in SEC regulations, and the reduced disclosure requirements applicable to smaller reporting companies may make our common stock less attractive to investors.
General Risk Factors
Our industry is subject to extensive government regulation and the imposition of additional regulations, which could materially harm our future earnings.
We may engage in litigation with our franchisees.
We operate in a highly competitive industry and may be unable to retain clients or market share.
paragraphs: Our common stock value and our business, results of operations, cash flows, and financial condition are subject to various risks, including, but not limited to, those set forth below. If any of these risks actually occur, the value of our common stock, business, results of operations, cash flows, and financial condition could be materially adversely affected. In such case, the value of your investment could decline, and you may lose all or part of the money you paid to buy our common stock. These risk factors should be carefully considered together with the other information in this Form 10-K, including the risks and uncertainties described under the heading "Special Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements."
We intend to continue making acquisitions a part of our growth initiative, and face the following risks in connection with this initiative:
Our strategy may be impeded, and we may not achieve our long-term growth goals if acquisition candidates are not available under acceptable terms.

We may have difficulty integrating acquired companies into our business, including our operational software and financial reporting systems, and may not effectively manage or (if deemed necessary) divest acquired companies to achieve expected growth. As previously reported, we identified a material weakness in our internal control over financial reporting related to insufficient accounting resources to handle the volume and complexity of technical accounting matters and to maintain adequate review procedures and segregation of duties. We have since remediated this material weakness and have concluded that the material weakness was effectively remediated as of December 31, 2025. However, there can be no assurance that we will not identify additional material weaknesses or significant deficiencies in the future, particularly as we continues to grow through acquisitions. Further information regarding this material weakness and its remediation is included in "Item 9A. Controls and Procedures" of this Form 10-K.
Acquisitions financed through equity offerings may cause dilution to our existing shareholders.
Acquisitions we announce could be viewed negatively by investors, which may adversely affect the price of our common stock.

paragraphs: HireQuest, Inc. (包含其子公司在內，簡稱 "本公司"、"我們"、"我們" 或 "我們的") 為一間設立於華盛頓州的德拉瓦州公司，原為 Command Staffing, LLC，於 2002 年成立。2005 年，Temporary Financial Services, Inc.（一間上市公司）取得 Command Staffing, LLC 的資產，並將合併後的公司更名為 Command Center, Inc. 2019 年 9 月 11 日，Command Center, Inc. 重新註冊為德拉瓦州公司，並更名為 HireQuest, Inc.，隨後取得 Hire Quest Holdings, LLC（簡稱 "Hire Quest Holdings"，與其子公司 Hire Quest, LLC 合稱 "Legacy HQ"）。此筆取得行動有時被稱為 "合併"。Hire Quest, LLC 於 2002 年成立為一間佛羅裏達州有限責任公司。Hire Quest Holdings, LLC 於 2017 年成立為一間佛羅裏達州有限責任公司。自合併後，我們進行了數筆取得行動，詳情請參閱下文。
我們的普通股於納斯達克市場交易，代碼為 "HQI"。所有提及 "普通股" 皆指 HireQuest, Inc. 的普通股，每股面值為 0.001 美元。
我們的總部位於南卡羅來納州 Goose Creek 的 111 Springhall Drive，郵遞區號 29445，電話號碼為 (843) 723-7400。更多關於我們的資訊可至 www.hirequest.com 查閱。本網站的資訊未於本年度報告 10-K 中引用。

2023 年 12 月 4 日，我們依照 2023 年 10 月 23 日簽訂的資產買斷協議，完成取得亞拉巴馬州十個 TEC Staffing Services（簡稱 "TEC"）據點，總價約為 9.8 百萬美元。TEC 自 1980 年代起，即為西北及中亞拉巴馬州僱主與勞工提供工業人力派遣服務。我們以現金及現有信貸線提款資助此筆取得行動。我們立即與現有特許經營商簽訂三份特許經營協議，並出售所取得的營運資產。

2024 年 12 月 30 日，我們依照 2024 年 12 月 13 日簽訂的資產買斷協議，完成取得科羅拉多州 Denver 的一個 Ready Temporary Services（簡稱 "RTS"）據點，總價為 1.4 百萬美元。RTS 自多個十年來，為科羅拉多州 Denver 的僱主與勞工提供日工與工業人力派遣服務。我們以現金及現有信貸線提款資助此筆取得行動。我們立即與特許經營商簽訂特許經營協議，並出售所取得的非營運資產。

2025 年 12 月 1 日，HQ MRI Corporation（簡稱 "HQ MRI"，為本公司之全資子公司）與 MRINetwork Operations, LLC（簡稱 "MRI Operations"）簽訂一項貢獻協議（簡稱 "貢獻協議"），生效日期為 2026 年 1 月 1 日（簡稱 "生效日"）。根據貢獻協議，HQ MRI 同意轉讓，MRI Operations 同意接受，與 MRINetwork 在生效日相關的資產與負債，作為交換，MRI Operations 向 HQ MRI 發行 MRI Operations 40% 的所有權單位。HQ MRI 轉讓 MRINetwork 所需的非合約人力派遣資產，以維持日常營運，與 MRINetwork 特許經營商的特許經營協議，與供應商及服務提供者的契約，所有與轉讓資產相關的對第三方主張之權利，保証、賠償及類似權利，與 HQ MRI 員工的契約，及其他附屬資產。MRI Operations 同時承擔網路員工的應計但未支付薪資與福利，所有來自網路日常營運的負債，包括應付帳款，以及與轉讓資產相關的負債。MRI Operations 剩餘 60% 的所有權由一位個人及四名現有 MRINetwork 特許經營商持有。此筆交易於 2026 年 1 月 1 日完成。MRINetwork 的合約人力派遣資產未於交易中轉讓，並完全由 HQ MRI 保留。
我們為全國性的人力派遣特許經營商，提供直接派遣及商業人力派遣解決方案，服務輕工業與藍領產業，並提供專業招聘辦公室，提供高階、管理及行政領域的永久聘僱服務。自合併後，我們開始擁有強大的直接派遣方案。透過 Snelling 取得行動與 LINK 取得行動，我們大幅擴展了傳統的商業人力派遣解決方案。
小型取得行動幫助我們填補據點，為特許經營商與客戶提供具針對性的服務。這些補充性取得行動也協助我們在某些地理區域強化現有服務。

2025 年，我們的加盟者在「HireQuest Direct」「Snelling」「DriverQuest」「HireQuest Health」「Northbound Executive Search」「Management Recruiters International」「TradeCorp」及「Sales Consultants」等商標下運作。HireQuest Direct 聚焦於每日工作/每日薪資的工作，主要服務建設與輕工業客戶。Snelling 與 HireQuest 聚焦於輕工業與行政領域的長期人力配置。TradeCorp 聚焦於建設工地技工類工作。DriverQuest 專門從事商業與非 CDL 司機，服務多樣產業與應用場景。HireQuest Health 專注於醫療與牙科產業的專業人力。Northbound、MRI 與 Sales Consultants 聚焦於高階、管理與專業人才的招募服務，雖然許多加盟者也提供短期顧問與合約人力服務。

我們的營業收入，主要由我們加盟據點運作所產生的加盟費、授權費以及對逾期應收款項收取的利息組成，2025 年為 30.6 百萬美元。此數字不包含我們目前所有之據點收入，因為這些據點被歸類為持有待售，並列為已終止營運。我們的系統總銷售額，我們定義為所有據點的銷售額，無論是我們所有並營運或由加盟者所有並營運，2025 年為 500.2 百萬美元。幾乎所有系統總銷售額來自加盟者所有之據點。我們在 2025 年僱用了約 75 千名臨時員工，並與 85 名獨立承包商合作。2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們擁有 413 家加盟者所有之據點與 1 家公司所有之據點，運作於 43 個州、華盛頓特區與 14 個美國以外國家。其中 197 家據點由 177 家加盟者經營，為 MRI 擁有之據點，於 2026 年 1 月 1 日出售給 MRINetwork Operations, LLC。淨計，我們在 2025 年關閉了 12 家據點（增加 7 家與關閉 19 家）。此外，還有 16 家 MRI 擁有之據點僅提供合約人力服務。
我們提供現有加盟者激勵措施，包括協助啟動資金與收購成本，以鼓勵他們拓展至新市場與產業。雖然人力派遣產業成長速度超過總體經濟與就業成長，但產業仍僅僱用美國非農業勞動力的一小部分。我們認為，目前僅有少數勞動力為臨時性僱用，加上未來總體經濟可能朝向更多臨時性僱用的趨勢，為未來內生性成長提供了有意義的機會。
我們的差異化服務由三個關鍵要素驅動：
本地所有與專注回應。我們的據點為加盟者所有。我們認為，在客戶互動大多發生的本地層級擁有權，使我們的組織更具靈活性與回應客戶需求的能力。由於加盟者對其據點的成功有個人財務利益，客戶與代表互動時，該代表有動機提供優質客戶服務並迅速解決問題。此外，加盟者因缺乏人員流動性，能建立長期關係。我們認為，本地所有與正確對齊的激勵措施結合，能提升客戶滿意度與提高客戶留存率。
我們據點直接派遣員工。我們建設與輕工業部門的大多數員工每日均由我們據點派遣。這使加盟者及其員工能為員工篩選工作、提供必要的個人防護裝備、協助員工安排彼此間的交通，並確保在正確時間派遣正確數量的合格人員。我們認為，員工由加盟據點派遣能提高一致性，因為員工可直接派往特定工地，而無需依賴電話等較不可靠的驗證方式。一旦我們與客戶與特定員工建立良好關係，我們有時會直接派遣這些員工至客戶場地。

headings: 與我們業務及產業相關之風險
併購可能對我們之業務產生不利影響。
新業務策略將導致我們增加支出，並可能對我們之核心業務產生不利影響。
我們已並可能持續無法吸引足夠之合適人選以滿足客戶之所有需求。
我們易受季節性波動影響，冬季月份之需求較低。
我們依賴極少數之個人，這些個人構成我們目前之管理層。
我們之營運及財務結果 largely 連結至我們之大型員工補償備抵，該備抵可能波動。
我們可能產生與僱用相關之聲請或其它類型之聲請及成本，這些聲請及成本可能對我們之業務造成重大損害。
若我們未能成功執行成長策略，包括現有及新加盟商的辦公室開發，將可能不利於我們增加營業收入及營運獲利的能力。
產業的變化可能對我們的管理階層、員工、資訊系統及內部控製造成壓力，可能對我們的業務產生負面影響。
對臨時僱用勞動力態度的改變可能對我們的營運結果及財務狀況產生負面影響。
與我們信貸協議及流動性相關的風險
我們的負債水平及信貸協議中的限制條款可能對我們的營運產生負面影響，並限制我們的流動性及應對經濟變動的能力。
此外，信貸協議中的信貸線條限制，包括但不限於我們的以下能力：
若流動性不足，我們可能無法追求具有吸引力的業務機會。
我們可能無法以有利條件取得用以支應營運資金、收購、資本、股息及其他需求的融資。
與我們特許經營商及商業模式相關的風險
將本公司自有辦公室轉為特許經營模式具有多重風險。
我們的營運與財務結果及成長策略與特許經營商的成功密切相關。
我們的特許經營商可能會採取可能損害我們業務的行動。
若我們未能識別、招募並與足夠數量的合格特許經營商簽訂協議，我們開設新辦公室及增加收入的能力可能會受到重大不利影響。
在現有市場開設新辦公室及積極拓展可能削減現有銷售，並可能對現有辦公室的銷售及與現有特許經營商的關係產生負面影響。
我們的許多特許經營權由極少數個人所控制。
我們的營運結果可能因某些特許經營商能否償還對我們的貸款而受到重大影響。
本公司成長策略依賴於尋找買主以處分所取得之業務資產。
本公司可能未恰當衡量與Franchise Expansion Incentive Program相關之成本與效益。
與科技及網路安全相關之風險
本公司機密及專屬資訊之不當揭露或遭未經授權存取，或未能充分保護此類資訊，可能對本公司業務造成重大損害。
本公司資訊科技系統可能需要更新或更換，此過程可能造成幹擾且費用高昂。若本公司未能依需求更新或更換資訊科技系統，可能對業務造成損害。
科技進步可能幹擾勞動力及招募市場。
本公司廠區、營運及資訊科技系統可能面臨損壞及中斷之風險。
本公司股票之持有相關風險
若本公司被視為「個人持有公司」，則可能需支付個人持有公司稅，此稅務負擔將對本公司現金流、營運成果及財務狀況產生不利影響。
本公司董事、高階管理人員及現有主要股東持有本公司普通股之大比例股份，可能限制其他股東對公司決策之影響力。
本公司股票每日交易量通常偏低，可能導致流動性不足、價格波動或股價低迷。
覆蓋本公司股票之分析師可能對本公司股票之價格及交易量產生負面影響。
若本公司停止支付普通股之現金股息，股東可能無法獲得投資回報，除非將普通股出售給價格高於購入價格之買方。
本公司根據 SEC 規範被歸類為「小型報告公司」，適用於小型報告公司之簡化揭露要求，可能使本公司普通股對投資者而言較不具吸引力。
一般風險因素
本公司所屬產業受政府嚴格規範，且可能增加更多規範，此等規範可能對本公司未來獲利產生重大不利影響。

paragraphs: 本公司普通股價值及業務、營運成果、現金流及財務狀況受多種風險影響，包括但不限於下列風險。若任何上述風險實際發生，將可能對本公司普通股價值、業務、營運成果、現金流及財務狀況造成重大不利影響。在此情況下，投資人所投資的價值可能下跌，並可能喪失全部或部分已支付購入本公司普通股的金額。這些風險因素應與本表10-K文件中其他資訊一併審慎考量，包括在「特別注意前瞻性陳述」標題下所描述的風險與不確定性。
本公司有意繼續將收購作為成長計畫的一部分，並在與此計畫相關方面面臨以下風險：
若收購目標無法在可接受條件下取得，本公司策略可能受阻，且無法達成長期成長目標。

本公司可能在將收購公司整合至本公司業務時遇到困難，包括作業軟體及財務報表系統，且可能無法有效管理或（如認為必要）出售收購公司以達成預期成長。如先前所報導，本公司已識別出在財務報導內部控制上的一項重大弱點，與處理技術會計事項的會計資源不足，以及維持適當審查程序及職務分離的措施不足有關。本公司已針對此重大弱點進行改善，並結論認為此重大弱點已在2025年12月31日有效改善。然而，無法保證本公司未來不會識別出其他重大弱點或重要缺失，特別是在本公司持續透過收購成長的情況下。有關此重大弱點及其改善措施的進一步資訊，請參閱本表10-K文件中的「項目9A. 控制與程序」。
透過發行普通股資助的收購可能導致現有股東的股權稀釋。
本公司所宣佈的收購可能被投資人視為負面，這可能會對本公司普通股的價格造成不利影響。
